s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass measured 12 cm and was non-tender
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Noted the lesion two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
Denied pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Medical history notable for hypertension and hysterectomy in 2016
Post-menopausal with no history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam was unremarkable
Pelvic exam was otherwise normal
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Routine laboratory results were within normal limits

differentials: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
per_call: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck

shortlist.label: Canal of Nuck hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the leading preoperative impression and ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Vulvar lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a large, painless mass in the vulvar region

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause a painless vulvar mass, although less common than lipoma

shortlist.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, it is a rare but important diagnosis to consider in a post-menopausal woman

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, gradually enlarging vulvar mass extending into the inguinal region, along with ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal, is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, especially given the preoperative impression and the absence of signs of malignancy or inflammation.

rejected.label: Vulvar lipoma
rejected.why: While possible, the mass's extension into the inguinal canal and the ultrasound description are less typical for a lipoma.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: This condition often presents with a larger, more infiltrative mass and can be associated with symptoms due to its locally aggressive nature, which doesn't fit the patient's asymptomatic presentation.

rejected.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
rejected.why: These are typically smaller, well-circumscribed masses that might not explain the extension into the inguinal canal as described.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The absence of symptoms such as pain, infection, or bleeding, and the lack of suspicious findings on ultrasound, make this less likely compared to a benign condition like a Canal of Nuck hernia.
